artist.heading: creative technologist, XR developer, and web developer
body: I build interactive systems where spatial interfaces, web engineering, and visual storytelling meet. My work moves between XR prototypes, browser-based experiences, research-driven interfaces, and visual narratives.

This portfolio is shaped as a working studio reel: technical enough for engineering review, visual enough for creative collaboration, and direct enough for HCI, XR, and creative technology opportunities.

items.title: Creative Technologist
items.description: Blend visual design, interaction concepts, and hands-on making to shape expressive digital experiences and portfolio-ready prototypes.

projects.title: Qianfan One Scroll
projects.summary: A noir-inspired visual system for a tabletop mystery experience, combining bold interface layouts, character art, and case-material storytelling.

projects.detailHeading: A tabletop mystery visual system built from noir contrast, annotated evidence, and character-driven interface art.
detailBody: Qianfan One Scroll uses bold graphic composition, case-material layouts, and illustrated player characters to frame a tabletop reasoning experience.
The project works well as the portfolio's visual narrative anchor because it shows art direction, UI composition, and story-facing design in one media-heavy package.

projects.title: Midnight at the Pagoda
projects.summary: I designed and prototyped a VR heritage tour, then turned it into a research environment to study how interacting with virtual artifacts affects memory retention.
projects.alt: Rendered pagoda exhibition scene with warm interior lighting and red architectural elements
projects.tagline: Tagline slot: a one-sentence project hook will go here.
projects.detailHeading: A VR gamified historical tour exploring artifact interaction and memory retention inside the Great Bao'en Temple Glazed Pagoda.
projects.overviewHeading: A VR heritage tour that turns the Great Bao'en Temple's layered history into an embodied climb through memory, artifacts, and space.
projects.overview: A Midnight at the Pagoda is a VR gamified historical tour originally developed in response to the 2024 Digital Heritage Hackathon brief for the Great Bao'en Temple Museum. Players climb the Glazed Pagoda of the Great Bao'en Temple from the lower levels to the top, interacting with museum artifacts on each floor. Through these encounters, they gradually uncover the history of the temple's construction, cultural significance, and layered material heritage.
detailBody: A Midnight at the Pagoda is a VR gamified historical tour originally developed in response to the 2024 Digital Heritage Hackathon brief for the Great Bao'en Temple Museum. Players climb the Glazed Pagoda of the Great Bao'en Temple from the lower levels to the top, interacting with museum artifacts on each floor. Through these encounters, they gradually uncover the history of the temple's construction, cultural significance, and layered material heritage.

The project began as a hackathon prototype for a VR museum experience. The design translated the Great Bao'en Temple's historical narrative into a vertical climbing journey, using the pagoda's floor-by-floor structure as both spatial progression and storytelling framework. Each level introduced interactive artifacts that acted as narrative anchors, allowing players to learn through movement, inspection, and embodied interaction rather than passive reading.

I later extended the prototype into an experimental environment for my Goldsmiths dissertation. The study used the VR scene to investigate whether interacting with virtual artifacts could improve users' memory retention of the historical context represented by those artifacts. This shifted the project from a cultural heritage prototype into a research tool for studying how embodied interaction may support learning, recall, and contextual understanding in immersive museum experiences.

The project was also developed further through my SJTU thesis as an exhibition-ready proposal, expanding the VR concept into a broader curatorial and visitor experience framework. While the proposal considered spatial storytelling, exhibition flow, and interpretive design, the portfolio focus remains on the VR prototype and research experiment as the project's core creative technology contribution.

projects.title: Self-Guided VR Onboarding for Classroom English Learning
projects.summary: Teaching the Body Language of a VR Learning App
projects.alt: GAVIS onboarding thumbnail with VR headset user and floating video panel
projects.tagline: Teaching the Body Language of a VR Learning App
projects.detailHeading: A self-guided Unity VR onboarding scene that teaches students the body language of GAVIS before login.
projects.overviewHeading: From staff-guided first use to a guided rehearsal inside the headset.
projects.overview: GAVIS needed a first-use path that could work in a shared classroom headset. I implemented the Unity onboarding scene that teaches pinch, controller use, review, and safety before students reach login.
detailBody: GAVIS needed a first-use path that could work in a shared classroom headset. I implemented the Unity onboarding scene that teaches pinch, controller use, review, and safety before students reach login.
My work covered scene setup, prefab setup, flow logic, condition validation, gesture animation production, feedback triggers, review navigation, headset QA, and performance validation.

detailSections.title: First Use Needed a Human Guide
body: In the MVP, students entered login directly. Many did not know what GAVIS expected, when to put down controllers, how to pinch, or how to stay safe without staff beside them.
A passive video helped explain the idea, but it did not reliably become action. The new scene needed to make learners rehearse the interaction inside VR.

mediaSlot.label: Slot 1 / before-after flow
mediaSlot.caption: Suggested visual: headset on -> guided onboarding -> validated interaction -> login.

detailSections.title: Teach By Doing
body: The core strategy was Condition-Gated Progression: students advance only after completing the intended physical or UI action.
That turns onboarding into a capability arc: understand GAVIS, use hands, pinch, select UI, review steps, learn safety rules, then enter the app.

mediaSlot.label: Slot 2 / learner capability arc
mediaSlot.caption: Suggested visual: a seven-step capability ladder from app intro to login handoff.

detailSections.title: A Validated Practice Loop
body: Each task panel combines a prompt, a validator, hint audio, success feedback, and progression. The scene waits when the learner struggles and confirms the moment when they succeed.
For the pinch target step, success is visible, audible, and spatial: target guidance, hand animation, success audio, VFX at the pinch position, UI state, and panel progression.

mediaSlot.label: Slot 3 / condition-gated pinch clip
mediaSlot.caption: Suggested visual: the learner completes pinch and receives multimodal success feedback.

detailSections.title: XR Animation Built Inside Unity
body: The hardest craft problem was gesture guidance. I built an in-Unity recording workflow instead of relying on a traditional Blender animation pipeline.
I recorded hand and controller motion in Play Mode, mapped trajectories, improved sampling and interpolation, then baked reusable clips for pinch and controller-down guidance.

mediaSlot.label: Slot 4 / animation workflow
mediaSlot.caption: Suggested visual: Play Mode recording, sampled motion, baked clip, final gesture animation.

detailSections.title: Built For Pilot Use
body: I structured the scene around flow orchestration, panel lifecycle, condition validators, navigation, feedback, remote-control hooks, and final login handoff.
The scene was tested hands-on with lab participants and education-sector stakeholders. On-device checks showed frame rate above the required threshold and RAM under 700 MB in a 10-minute playback.

mediaSlot.label: Slot 5 / QA and pilot evidence
mediaSlot.caption: Suggested visual: headset QA notes, pilot walkthrough, or a performance validation capture.
